content: Senna acutifolia, also known as Alexandrian senna, Egyptian senna, Séné de la palthe, Tinnevelly senna, or East Indian senna, is an ornamental plant belonging to the genus Senna. This shrubby plant can grow up to two meters in height and features branched, pale-colored stems. It is native to Upper Egypt, particularly in the Nubian region, and is also found near Khartoum, Sudan, where it is cultivated for commercial purposes. Additionally, it is grown in India and Somalia. The name Alexandrian senna originates from the historical role of Alexandria as a major trade port. In the past, the fruits and leaves of this plant were transported from Nubia, Sudan, and other regions to Alexandria, and from there, they were distributed across the Mediterranean Sea to Europe and neighboring parts of Asia. The leaves of Senna acutifolia are compound and feathery, arranged in pairs. Each leaf consists of 4 to 6 pairs of leaflets, which are fully edged and have sharp tips. The midribs of the leaflets are symmetrically divided at their base. The flowers of this plant grow in racemes, with the blossoms located internally. These flowers are large, yellow in color, and tend to develop a brownish hue over time. The fruits of the plant are flat, compressed, and horned in shape.
